simple.meaning: אַרְנֶבֶת (ʼarnebeth) is a Hebrew word meaning “the hare.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַרְנֶבֶת (H768) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 11:6, with occurrences in Leviticus, Deuteronomy.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַרְנֶבֶת (H768) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַרְנֶבֶת (ʼarnebeth) / H768 is traced through Leviticus 11:6, Deuteronomy 14:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H768. arnebeth אַרְנֶבֶת noun feminine hare (Arabic , Syriac , Assyrian annabu , as springer? ) eating of it forbidden Lev 11:6 (P) Deut 14:7 . אָ֫נֶה אָ֫נָה see below אַי .

occurrences.englishText: The hare, because it chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, is unclean to you.

Nevertheless these you shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of those who have the hoof split: the camel, the hare, and the rabbit. Because they chew the cud but don’t part the hoof, they are unclean to you.
